A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DenoiseRotator and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original material can be matched reliably, including v1 Appendix D, retained as v2 Appendix G.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments measuring perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, entropy reduction, and inference time, with extensive additional benchmark results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds learning-rate sensitivity, block-diagonal rotation, and LoRA fine-tuning experiments in Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: The entropy objective, rotation placement, QR parameterization, and main pruning pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix E adds an optional block-diagonal replacement for dense rotations, and Appendix F adds post-pruning LoRA fine-tuning with frozen rotation matrices. These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: Both versions cover WikiText-2, C4, and the same five zero-shot tasks. The added studies use the already evaluated LLaMA-3-8B model and existing task coverage. Using the WikiText-2 training split for LoRA changes the training protocol, not the represented domain or task.

E2.justification: Magnitude, Wanda, and SparseGPT remain the evaluated pruning comparators, with unchanged membership in the retained comparisons. LoRA is evaluated as an additional stage of the proposed pipeline, rather than an independent competing method. The newly cited mixed-sparsity pruning work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The original benchmark protocols remain unchanged, but v2 substantially extends the experimental design: Appendix D crosses four learning rates with six training budgets, Appendix E varies rotation block counts, and Appendix F introduces recovery fine-tuning after 100 rotation-training steps using 4096 WikiText-2 training sequences of length 2048. These are additional protocols, not revisions to the original 2000-step benchmark setting.

E4.justification: v1 already includes an optimization-step ablation and inference-overhead analysis. v2 expands sensitivity testing across learning rates and steps, tests the accuracy–cost trade-off from restricting rotation blocks, and examines compatibility with post-pruning LoRA. Appendices D–F substantially broaden the questions investigated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The accuracy fluctuations discussed in v2 Appendix D concern different hyperparameter configurations and do not constitute run-to-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained, including v1 Tables 8–22 as v2 Tables 11–25. New Tables 8–10 add substantial results. Table 9 reports that increasing blocks from 1 to 8 reduces time per step from 0.124 to 0.072 seconds while perplexity worsens from 7.597 to 8.882. Table 10 reports LoRA recovery from 14.31 to 9.32 perplexity and 60.67% to 61.08% accuracy in the new 100-step rotation setting, not an update to the original 2000-step results.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds a quantitative complexity claim: using b equal orthogonal blocks of width hidden_size/b reduces storage and computation to 1/b of the dense requirements. No supporting proof is added. The original entropy formulation, invariance derivation, and QR argument remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's explicit claim that the method is model-agnostic, modestly narrowing its advertised applicability. The central claims about entropy-guided importance concentration, compatibility with pruning methods, and empirical benefits remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 removes v1's interpretation that declining zero-shot accuracy suggests generation-task overfitting. Appendix D instead discusses accuracy fluctuations without a clear linear relationship to perplexity. Appendices E–F add interpretations concerning computational trade-offs and fine-tuning stability. The stated semi-structured-sparsity limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added studies' hardware and block construction, plus a detailed LoRA configuration: rank 8, alpha 32, dropout 0.1, learning rate 2e-4, weight decay 1e-2, Adam, a linear scheduler, 400 warm-up steps, and frozen rotations. These supplement the retained implementation details; the code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Hu et al.'s LoRA and Shao et al.'s one-shot sensitivity-aware mixed-sparsity pruning. The positioning relative to SliceGPT, QuaRot, SpinQuant, and RotPruner remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. v2 adds Appendices D–F and acknowledgements, relabels the existing results appendix as G, updates cross-references, and makes localized abstract and experimental-discussion edits. There is no extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables for hyperparameter sensitivity, block configurations, and LoRA recovery. Existing figures and table designs are retained; the original appendix results are relocated and renumbered. Other changes are limited to emphasis, conference formatting, and page layout.

improvement.justification: Appendices D–F provide useful evidence beyond v1's limited step ablation: broader hyperparameter sensitivity, measured accuracy–cost trade-offs, and a documented LoRA recovery example. Removing the model-agnostic claim also improves scope calibration. The gains are limited because the new studies concern one model and provide no repeated-run uncertainty; the LoRA comparison also lacks a Wanda-plus-LoRA control to substantiate its stronger training-stability interpretation.
